AI.description: AI-oriented samples that combine model calls, search, and database-backed application workflows.
AI.useWhen: Use when an application needs grounded AI features close to operational data.

APEX.description: Browser-based application development and workspace setup served through ORDS.
APEX.useWhen: Use when local Oracle AI Database stacks need low-code app screens or SQL workspace access.

Duality Views.description: Document-shaped access over relational tables using JSON Relational Duality Views.
Duality Views.useWhen: Use when APIs need JSON documents without giving up relational storage, SQL, constraints, and transactions.

Graph.description: Connected-data modeling and querying for relationships, paths, and networks.
Graph.useWhen: Use when recommendations, lineage, impact analysis, or traversal-heavy screens matter.

GraphQL.description: GraphQL-style query access for clients that need shaped responses from database data.
GraphQL.useWhen: Use when API consumers should ask for exactly the fields and relationships they need.

JMS.description: Java Message Service samples backed by Oracle AI Database transactional event queues.
JMS.useWhen: Use when Java services need durable messaging with familiar JMS APIs.

JPA.description: Java persistence samples for mapping application entities to Oracle AI Database tables.
JPA.useWhen: Use when Spring or Jakarta applications need ORM-based relational persistence.

Indexing.description: Index examples that make JSON, text, vector, and spatial queries practical at application scale.
Indexing.useWhen: Use when a query pattern is correct but needs a database-native access path before it is production-shaped.

JSON.description: Document-shaped data and SQL/JSON querying inside Oracle AI Database.
JSON.useWhen: Use when records need flexible structure without leaving SQL, indexes, constraints, and transactions.

Kafka.description: Kafka-compatible eventing and migration paths backed by Oracle AI Database queues.
Kafka.useWhen: Use when comparing separate-broker designs or moving Kafka-shaped workloads toward database-native eventing.

MCP.description: Model Context Protocol samples that connect agents and tools to Oracle AI Database workflows.
MCP.useWhen: Use when AI tools need controlled access to SQL, metadata, or database-backed operations.

MongoDB.description: MongoDB-compatible API access over Oracle AI Database data through ORDS.
MongoDB.useWhen: Use when an existing document app expects MongoDB-style APIs but the data should stay in Oracle AI Database.

Observability.description: Tracing and client metadata samples for following application work into database sessions.
Observability.useWhen: Use when teams need to correlate HTTP, JDBC, JMS, and database activity during operations.

OCI.description: Cloud integration samples that connect Oracle AI Database applications with OCI services.
OCI.useWhen: Use when local samples need to reflect deployment, secrets, or service integration patterns on OCI.

ORDS.description: Oracle REST Data Services samples for exposing database-backed APIs.
ORDS.useWhen: Use when clients need REST, MongoDB-compatible, or service-style access without owning low-level SQL.

Oracle Text.description: Full-text indexing and search over relational and JSON data.
Oracle Text.useWhen: Use when keyword search, text filters, and document relevance need to run beside transactional data.

PDB.description: Pluggable database samples for isolating services or workloads inside Oracle AI Database.
PDB.useWhen: Use when each service needs a stronger database boundary without running separate database servers.

PL/SQL.description: Database-side procedural logic for transactions, queues, and operational workflows.
PL/SQL.useWhen: Use when business logic benefits from running close to the data and inside the transaction.

SpringBoot.description: Spring Boot samples for persistence, configuration, messaging, tracing, and service integration.
SpringBoot.useWhen: Use when Java services need common Spring patterns backed by Oracle AI Database.

SQLcl.description: Command-line and agent workflows built around SQLcl access to Oracle AI Database.
SQLcl.useWhen: Use when developers or tools need scriptable SQL access, local automation, or MCP-backed database work.

Testcontainers.description: Disposable Oracle AI Database Free containers for repeatable local and integration tests.
Testcontainers.useWhen: Use when tests need real database behavior without sharing a long-lived development instance.

TxEventQ.description: Transactional queues for database-backed events and messaging.
TxEventQ.useWhen: Use when event delivery and data changes need the same transaction boundary.

Vector Search.description: Store embeddings and search records by semantic similarity.
Vector Search.useWhen: Use when users search by meaning or AI answers need grounded records.

microservices.description: Service-boundary samples that keep application ownership and database access explicit.
microservices.useWhen: Use when teams are splitting responsibilities across services without losing transactional clarity.

security.description: Security-related samples for secrets, access boundaries, and safer application configuration.
security.useWhen: Use when database-backed applications need environment-aware secrets or tighter operational controls.

Spatial.description: Location-aware storage, indexing, and spatial queries over geometry data.
Spatial.useWhen: Use when products ask about proximity, containment, routing, zones, or other location behavior.
